title: 341 - Final Fantasy
method: claude-code: written from the transcript, links verified by script

items.name: Final Fantasy
items.description: The episode's game: Square's 1987 JRPG, released in North America in 1990, with a party of four chosen classes.

items.name: Square
items.description: The developer of Final Fantasy, rumored to have named the game because it was their last attempt.

items.name: Fighting Fantasy
items.description: The title the creators reportedly considered, which became Final Fantasy.

items.name: Final Fantasy XVI
items.description: The newest mainline entry, credited with returning the series to prestige.

items.name: Final Fantasy VII Remake
items.description: The remake series that, with FFXVI, helped restore the franchise's standing.

items.name: Final Fantasy XV
items.description: Entry hoped to be a return to form, with four friends traveling by car.

items.name: Final Fantasy VII
items.description: The 1997 PlayStation game that introduced two of the hosts to the series.

items.name: PlayStation
items.description: Sony's console, on which a Final Fantasy VII demo disc was a first exposure to the series.

links.label: Wikipedia: PlayStation (console)
links.note: Home video game console by Sony

items.name: Final Fantasy VIII
items.description: The PlayStation game one host played for years, with a train mission and a tough boss.

items.name: Kingdom Hearts
items.description: Square Enix series that connects to Final Fantasy VIII, with its time loop and Disney crossover jokes.

items.name: Final Fantasy VI
items.description: Super Nintendo entry, played after Final Fantasy VII.

items.name: Final Fantasy IX
items.description: The PlayStation entry that dropped much of the sci-fi look.

items.name: Final Fantasy X
items.description: PlayStation 2 entry with a linear map and no overworld.

items.name: Final Fantasy XI
items.description: The online entry one host skipped.

items.name: Final Fantasy XII
items.description: Entry with the Gambit system, often defended as a hidden gem.

items.name: Super Smash Bros. Melee
items.description: GameCube game whose trophies sparked one host's interest in retro games.

items.name: Quest 64
items.description: N64 RPG that was one host's first, and a poor introduction to turn-based games.

items.name: Final Fantasy IV
items.description: Super Nintendo game, released in North America as Final Fantasy II, that hooked one host on the series.

items.name: Dragon Warrior
items.description: The earlier NES RPG with a single hero, compared to Final Fantasy's party.

items.name: Fax (Faxanadu)
items.description: A previous Essential-list NES action RPG, which one host used as a party member name.

items.name: Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!!
items.description: NES boxing game one host named a black belt party member after (Taiso).

items.name: Archon
items.description: Game one host named a black mage after.

links.label: Wikipedia: Archon: The Light and the Dark

items.name: Rygar
items.description: NES game one host named a white mage after.

items.name: Adventures in the Magic Kingdom
items.description: The earlier NES Disney game, compared to the town and castle layout in Corneria.

links.label: Wikipedia: Adventures in the Magic Kingdom

items.name: Earthbound
items.description: Super Nintendo RPG whose battles don't show your characters.

items.name: Pokémon Red and Blue
items.description: Games with known stat bugs, like attacks that can miss at 100 percent accuracy.

links.label: Wikipedia: Pokémon Red, Blue, and Yellow

items.name: Star Fox
items.description: Game whose first planet, Corneria, shares a name with Final Fantasy's first town.

items.name: Yoshitaka Amano
items.description: Final Fantasy's illustrator, whose gothic art contrasts with Dragon Warrior's cartoon style.

links.label: Wikipedia: Yoshitaka Amano
links.note: Japanese artist, character designer, and illustrator (born 1952)

items.name: Akira Toriyama
items.description: Dragon Ball creator who drew Dragon Warrior's characters.

items.name: Dungeons & Dragons
items.description: Tabletop RPG whose bestiary and rules heavily influenced Final Fantasy.

items.name: Nobunaga's Ambition
items.description: Strategy series compared to Final Fantasy's hidden stats.

items.name: Final Fantasy: Stranger of Paradise
items.description: Action RPG prequel that retells the Chaos story with Jack Garland.

links.label: Wikipedia: Stranger of Paradise: Final Fantasy Origin

items.name: Chrono Trigger
items.description: Super Nintendo RPG used as an example of a good final-boss reveal and ports with new dungeons.

items.name: Tetsuya Nomura
items.description: Final Fantasy and Kingdom Hearts designer, who reportedly wanted Final Fantasy XV to be a musical.

items.name: Nobuo Uematsu
items.description: The composer of Final Fantasy's music, praised throughout the episode.

items.name: The Black Mages
items.description: Rock band led by Uematsu that arranges Final Fantasy music.

items.name: Distant Worlds: Music from Final Fantasy
items.description: Live orchestral concert series of Final Fantasy music.

links.label: Wikipedia: Final Fantasy concerts
links.note: Concerts of music from the Final Fantasy video game series

items.name: Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within
items.description: Square's 2001 CG film that nearly sank the company.

links.label: Wikipedia: Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within

items.name: Final Fantasy Pixel Remaster
items.description: The remaster with auto-battle, encounter toggles and no Peninsula of Power.

links.label: Wikipedia: Final Fantasy Pixel Remaster
links.note: Series of Final Fantasy video game remasters

items.name: NEStalgia Essential Games List
items.description: The show's list of NES games that define the system; Final Fantasy was just voted in.
